log.text: POI placed: poi:bell-rope (feature) at loc:hollowmere-shore — hidden DC 12

The pebbles crunch under your boots as you come over the ridge, and then the reservoir opens below you — black and vast and wrong, the way standing water is always wrong when it used to be a valley full of houses.

The first toll comes up through the ground before it reaches your ears. Low. Muffled. Like a great throat clearing itself far, far beneath the water. The surface shivers in a single ripple, spreading outward from a point near the eastern weir — and then goes still again, as though it had never happened.

The shore is a crescent of wet pebbles. Stilted shacks lean over the water on either side, their shutters barred tight, no smoke from the chimneys, no light. A stone weir curves out to the east, and anchored to an iron ring at its base: a rope. Thick. Tarred black. It descends from the ring straight down into the reservoir without touching shore at all, taut as a bowstring, trembling faintly with each invisible movement below.

The mist sits on the water's surface and does not move.

Aldric — you've heard that sound before. Twelve years ago, from the far bank, through the noise of machinery and flooding sluices and a man screaming from a half-submerged bell tower. Your hands probably remember it before your mind does.

Every shutter on every shack is barred. But there's a light — thin, yellow, wavering — leaking from under the door of the boathouse at the water's edge.

What do you do?

adventure.pitch: A gothic tale of drowned debt: the mining town of Hollowmere was flooded to make a reservoir, sealing bell-founder Corvin Bell inside his own half-finished church. His masterwork bronze bell went down with him. Now, every night the bell tolls beneath the water and rises a little higher on its rope, and with each toll the drowned dead climb the rope toward the living. The debt owed him must be paid

scene:b1.title: The Rope on the Shore
scene:b1.summary: The party arrives at a shore hamlet of stilted shacks as the bell's first muffled toll shudders through the water. Fisherfolk cower behind barred doors; the boatwright Mother Sedge knows the old story. A slick bell-rope rises from the deep and is anchored to a stone weir. Investigate the rope (Perception DC 12 finds fresh drowned handprints climbing it), calm or bargain with Sedge (Persuasion DC 13 gets a boat and the drowned town's map), or hold the shore when the night's first climbers crest the water. Waterlogged dead haul themselves ashore at the toll.

scenePlan.look: A pebbled crescent shore under a stone weir; stilted shacks lean over black water, jetties jut into the reservoir, and a thick tarred rope climbs from the deep to an iron ring on the weir.
scenePlan.mood: grim indigo dusk, cold mist off the water
features: the tarred bell-rope rising from the wat

spec.brief: a pebbled crescent shore under a stone weir; stilted shacks lean over black water, jetties jut into the reservoir, and a thick tarred rope climbs from the deep to an iron ring on the weir
narrationOnly: the first muffled toll shuddering up through the water and into boots and bones
the smell of cold mildew and black silt rising off the reservoir
fresh drowned handprints on the tarred rope — visible only on close inspection (Perception DC 12)
fisherfolk voices hushed behind barred shutters
Mother Sedge's willingness to bargain: Persuasion DC 13 yields a diving-bell and the drowned town's map
the periodic rhythm of the bell's toll felt as pressure in the chest, not heard as sound above water

scene:b2.title: The Drowned Descent
scene:b2.summary: Following the rope down (or by Sedge's diving-bell), the party enters the flooded upper streets of Hollowmere — a canted, silt-choked ruin threaded with air-pockets in overturned houses. Navigate the maze of streets and trapped air (Survival/Investigation DC 13 to find breathable pockets and the church's bell-arch), avoid the drowned that drift like weeds, or lure them off with light and noise. Pip may recognize a smuggler's cache here — his family fled Hollowmere before the flood, leaving debts of their own. The clapper of the great bell was stolen and hidden in a submerged countinghouse.

scenePlan.look: A submerged grid of collapsed stone streets under black water, roofs broken open, a leaning countinghouse and the arched belfry-mouth of a half-sunk church at the far end.
scenePlan.mood: lightless green-black underwater gloom, drifting silt

spec.brief: a submerged grid of collapsed stone streets under black water, roofs broken open, a leaning countinghouse and the arched belfry-mouth of a half-sunk church at the far end
narrationOnly: the lightless green-black underwater gloom pressing on eyes and lungs
the Navigation/Investigation challenge to locate breathable air pockets in overturned houses (Survival DC 13)
Pip's moment of recognition: his family's name scratched into a beam of the countinghouse, debts unpaid before the flood
the tolling felt as deep bone-vibration through the water rather than heard as sound
the drowned drifters' passive drift becoming agitated when the party carries a light source — luring mechanic
the smell of silt and rot trapped in air pockets
the Survival/Investigation DC 13 required to navigate from the entry rope to the bell-arch without being lost in silt-out

scene:b3.title: The Founder in His Bell
scene:b3.summary: Inside the drowned church, the great bronze bell hangs mouth-down over the founder's sealed tomb; within it, wound in the rope, is Corvin Bell — a bloated, ringing revenant who tolls the dead upward with his own bones. Confront him. He can be laid to rest by returning the clapper and tolling the bell once in true mourning (Religion/Persuasion DC 15 acknowledges his debt), or destroyed outright (harder fight, curse lingers). Elara may read the founder's inscription (Arcana DC 14) revealing the toll is a debt-count, not malice. Aldric can brace the swinging bell against him. End it as the bell rings clean and the water stills.

scenePlan.look: A flooded stone church interior, roof half-gone to the surface light above; a colossal bronze bell hangs over a cracked founder's tomb, chains and a frayed rope coiling into its dark mouth.
scenePlan.mood: cathedral gloom lit by a single shaft of surface moonlight through broken roof

blueprint.premise: A gothic tale of drowned debt: the mining town of Hollowmere was flooded to make a reservoir, sealing bell-founder Corvin Bell inside his own half-finished church. His masterwork bronze bell went down with him. Now, every night the bell tolls beneath the water and rises a little higher on its rope, and with each toll the drowned dead climb the rope toward the living. The debt owed him must be paid
blueprint.centralProblem: The bell rises nightly, dragging the reservoir's dead upward; unless the party descends to the drowned church and settles the founder's debt (his body given rest, his bell's tongue silenced or restored), the flood-dead will overrun the shore hamlet.
blueprint.intendedEnding: The party reaches the sunken church, confronts the animate remains of Corvin Bell, and pays his debt — burying his bones, returning the stolen bell-clapper to hang the bell true, and tolling it once in honest mourning. The bell falls silent, the risen dead sink back, and the reservoir stills. If they merely destroy him, the tolling stops but the valley remains cursed water.
blueprint.opening: Dusk on the shingle shore of Weirwater Reservoir, at the drowned hamlet of Hollowmere, where a rotted bell-rope trails up out of the black water onto the beach — and something has been climbing it.

spine.intent: Party learns the bell rises and the dead climb its rope.
Party recovers the tool needed to pay the debt.
Founder laid to rest, bell rung true.
The reservoir falls silent; the drowned sink home and the valley is finally at peace.

brief.activeBeatIntent: On the shore, the party learns the tolling bell is climbing its rope and the drowned dead follow it upward — the debt owed to Corvin Bell must be reckoned before the hamlet is overrun.

reachable.hook: The wet rope descends into black water, still trembling with each toll — following it down is the only way to reach the church and whatever settles the debt.

clocks: Each nightfall the bell tolls and rises higher; the drowned climb nearer the shore.

brief.notes: No divergence yet. Plant early the twin truths — bury the bones AND return the stolen clapper — so the honest-mourning resolution stays reachable rather than a mere kill.

voice.want: To keep her surviving neighbours alive through one more night
voice.fear: That the toll is counting down to her own name

voice.want: his debt acknowledged and his bones given rest
voice.fear: being melted down and forgotten, unrung

poi:bell-rope.look: A thick tarred rope, cold and slick, rising from the black water — the surface around it disturbed in slow circles. Where your lantern catches it, you can make out dark smears on the weave: handprints, fresh, climbing upward.
poi:bell-rope.notes: Fresh drowned handprints on the rope — evidence the dead are already climbing. Tells the party the first wave is close.
